name: Is it safe to put my customer, subscriber, or business data into an AI workflow?
description: Only share the minimum information needed, use redacted test data, review provider settings and terms, limit account access, and document retention and deletion

mainEntity.name: Is it safe to put my customer, subscriber, or business data into an AI workflow?

acceptedAnswer.text:
Protect sensitive information by minimizing what the workflow receives, controlling permissions, reviewing the provider’s settings, and avoiding unnecessary personal or confidential data in prompts. AI convenience is not a reason to copy entire customer files, financial records, or private business documents into an unreviewed system.

Use placeholders or redacted examples while testing. Keep a written record of what data the workflow uses, where it goes, how long it is retained under the provider’s terms, and who can access the connected account.

Key factors:
- Sensitivity of the information
- Provider controls and account settings
- User permissions
- Retention and deletion practices

Ask whether the workflow truly needs each field before connecting it. Run My AI Business’s emphasis on secure account connections and human-directed automation provides a practical starting point for safer setup.
acceptedAnswer.description: Only share the minimum information needed, use redacted test data, review provider settings and terms, limit account access, and document retention and deletion practices. Avoid placing sensitive records into a workflow without understanding where the data goes.
